header.contentDescription: A graticule and six coastal landmarks drawn by latitude and longitude over the Blue Marble texture, to check that the two agree

drawTextAnchored.text: green line = the equator as latlon() draws it
red line = the prime meridian, longitude zero
If the mapping is right the green line follows the map's own equator, the red line runs down
through the Gulf of Guinea, and every pin sits on its own headland.
A constant gap is an offset. A gap that changes along the line is a distortion. They need
different fixes, which is why the earlier single-number corrections kept half-working.
drag to turn the globe. Every mark here is outward-facing, so anything round the back is culled.
does a place drawn by lat/lon land where the map puts it?
